title: Incident evidence chain and forensic runbook
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary
This runbook defines the incident evidence chain and forensic procedures for Redwood Inference. It describes what to preserve, how to collect evidence reliably, who owns each step, and how evidence is stored for post-incident analysis and regulatory review. The goal is to preserve actionable telemetry and system state without delaying customer-facing remediation or violating privacy controls.

When to use this document
- Use when an incident involves: data integrity questions, possible security compromise, unexplained model quality regressions, or any situation where later forensic analysis is required.
- If the incident is purely a transient metric blip with obvious root cause (e.g., planned capacity maintenance announced beforehand), follow the standard incident command playbook instead.

Principles
- Capture early: first 15 minutes matter.
- Minimize blast radius: collection should not exacerbate the incident.
- Chain of custody: every snapshot must be tagged with who collected it, why, and cryptographic checksums where feasible.
- Privacy-first: redact or avoid collecting customer PII unless absolutely required and approved by security/legal.

Roles and ownership
- Incident Commander (IC): overall owner of incident response and evidence decisions for the incident. Typical role: SRE on-call lead.
- Forensic Lead: security engineer or senior SRE responsible for evidence collection and preservation.
- Telemetry Engineer: owns access to observability tools (Datadog, Loki, Splunk) and runs bulk exports.
- Platform Engineer: runs live-system snapshots (heap/VM/gcore) where permissible.
- Legal & Security Liaison: approves sensitive evidence collection and external requests.

Immediate steps (0–15 minutes) — evidence-first checklist
1) Declare evidence mode: IC sets incident bridge topic and announces "EVIDENCE MODE" in the bridge, which signals minimal state mutation.
2) High-level metadata capture (IC or Forensic Lead):
   - Incident ID, start timestamp, primary affected service(s), customer-impact flag.
   - Save as incident-metadata.json. Example content: {
     "incident_id": "INC-20260120-1234",
     "start_ts": "2026-01-20T14:12:03Z"
   }
3) Telemetry snapshot (Telemetry Engineer):
   - Export 30m windows of relevant metrics and traces centered on detection time. Preferred formats: JSON for traces (Jaeger/Zipkin), CSV/JSON for metrics.
   - Command example (Datadog API):
     curl -s -X POST "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/query" "-d "{\'from\':<ts>,\'to\':<ts>}"" -H 'DD-API-KEY: <redacted>'
4) Logs (Telemetry Engineer):
   - Pull logs for implicated service instances for window (-30m, +30m). Use indexed queries and export to object store.
   - Example Loki query: {job="inference-runtime", level="ERROR"} |= "timeout" | json
   - Store exported logs at s3://redwood-forensics/<incident_id>/logs/
5) Live-system snapshot (Platform Engineer, with Forensic Lead approval):
   - When safe and necessary, capture: process list, open sockets (ss -tunap), GPU state (nvidia-smi -q), thread stacks (gdb/gcore), running containers (docker ps --no-trunc), and kernel dmesg.
   - Minimal command set:
     sudo ss -tunap > /tmp/<incident_id>-sockets.txt
     sudo nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/<incident_id>-gpu-state.xml
     sudo gcore -o /tmp/<incident_id>-pid <pid>  (only for root cause capture; avoid on high-latency prod tiers)
6) KV cache and model artifacts (Serving/Platform Engineer):
   - Snapshot model artifact versions, model config, and a checksum of model weights. Record quantization/serve pipeline used.
   - Example: sha256sum /opt/models/release-v12/model.bin > /tmp/<incident_id>-model-sha256.txt

Chain of custody and metadata tagging
- Every artifact stored in object store must be accompanied by a small metadata JSON that includes: collector, timestamp, purpose, commands-run, checksum, access-list.
- Naming convention: <incident_id>/<artifact_type>/<hostname>-<timestamp>-<short-hash>
- Example metadata file: /s3/redwood-forensics/INC-20260120-1234/logs/collector-metadata.json

Preservation and storage policy
- Short-term: all artifacts are immutable in s3://redwood-forensics/<incident_id>/ and preserved for 90 days.
- Long-term retention: items marked as legal evidence are moved to secure evidence vault with 7-year retention and HSM-backed checksums.
- Access control: default: read-by-role (Forensic Lead, IC, Legal, Security). Requests for other access must be logged and approved.

Evidence formats and minimum required fields
- Logs export (JSON lines): timestamp, host, service, level, trace_id, span_id, message, raw_payload (if allowed).
- Traces: full trace with spans; include span tags for model_id and request_size.
- Metrics: time-series with host and service dimensions labeled.
- Heap/core dumps: store compressed, provenance metadata, do not upload to public cloud without explicit approval.

Customer-facing communication templates (short, factual)
- Initial notice (when customer impact confirmed):
  Subject: Redwood Incident INC-{{incident_id}} – service impact
  Body: "We are investigating an issue affecting inference responses in region {{region}}. Our SRE team has activated evidence preservation and is working on restoration. No action is required from your side; we will follow up with timelines and mitigation steps within 60 minutes. If you need an incident contact, reply to this message."
- Investigation update (optional):
  "Update: We have captured necessary telemetry and isolated the affected fleet. A mitigation is in progress. We will provide a technical summary in the post-incident report."
- Post-incident summary: include non-sensitive findings, mitigation steps taken, and customer-facing remediation guidance. Avoid including raw logs or PII.

Post-incident process and postmortem requirements
1) Postmortem author: assigned by IC within 48 hours.
2) Required sections: summary, timeline, evidence artifacts list (with object store paths), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (with owners and due dates), verification plan.
3) Evidence appendix: list of preserved artifacts and their checksums (sha256).
4) Action items: track in the company issue tracker; every high/critical incident must have at least one preventative action with owner and ETA.

Forensic analysis playbook (when security compromise suspected)
- Immediately escalate to Security Liaison. Security will:
  - Freeze affected accounts and suspend automation that could mutate evidence.
  - Start a parallel secure evidence export into the secure evidence vault (encrypted with customer-specific KMS if necessary).
  - Collect network captures (only where lawful and approved): tcpdump on affected hosts with strict retention and access controls.
- Legal must be consulted before any external notifications that could disclose details of the investigation.

Automated capture scripts and examples
- We maintain a small toolbox in Git: infra/forensics-scripts. Key scripts:
  - capture-metrics-windows.sh: exports Datadog metrics to JSON and uploads to S3.
  - snapshot-service-state.py: collects ps, ss, docker/containerd metadata, nvidia-smi output, and zips artifacts.
Example capture-metrics-windows.sh (trimmed):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
INCID=$1
FROM_TS=$(date -u -d "-30 minutes" +%s)
TO_TS=$(date -u +%s)
curl -s -X POST "https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1/query" -H 'DD-API-KEY: $DD_API_KEY' -d "{\"from\":$FROM_TS,\"to\":$TO_TS}" > /tmp/${INCID}-metrics.json
aws s3 cp /tmp/${INCID}-metrics.json s3://redwood-forensics/${INCID}/metrics/${INCID}-metrics.json

Testing the runbook (game day plan)
- Quarterly game day: sim scenario where a model-serving node misbehaves and evidence must be preserved.
- Objectives: validate that telemetry exports complete in <15 minutes, that object store paths match metadata, and that access controls prevent unauthorized reads.
- Scoring rubric: completion of snapshots (30 pts), metadata completeness (30 pts), correct chain-of-custody (20 pts), successful postmortem with action items (20 pts).

Appendix A — quick commands and queries
- Export traces (Jaeger): curl -s "http://jaeger-query:16686/api/traces?service=inference-runtime&start=<start>&end=<end>" > /tmp/traces.json
- Loki bulk export example: loki_query='\"{job=\\\"inference-runtime\\\"} |= \\\"error\\\"\"'
  curl -G -s http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range --data-urlencode "query=$loki_query" --data-urlencode "start=$START" --data-urlencode "end=$END" > logs.json
- Compute sha256: sha256sum /opt/models/release-v12/model.bin > /tmp/model-sha256.txt

Appendix B — minimum SLOs for evidence procedures
- Telemetry snapshot completion: 95% of exports must complete within 15 minutes of request.
- Metadata attachment: 100% of artifacts uploaded to object store must have an accompanying metadata JSON.
- Chain-of-custody logging: every artifact access must be logged and retained for 180 days.

References and related docs
- See incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024 for parallel incident orchestration responsibilities.
- See eng-infra/retention-policies-2024 for data retention and deletion schedules.
